title: Line modules on split torus torsors over smooth schemes
statement: Let $k$ be a field [def-weil-field] and $X$ a smooth separated finite-type $k$-scheme [def-pc-scheme, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms, def-weil-finite-type-morphism]. Let $r\geq0$, put $T=(\mathbf G_{m,k})^r$, where $\mathbf G_{m,k}=\operatorname{Spec}k[t,t^{-1}]$, and let $q:Y\to X$ be a $T$-torsor. This means a faithfully flat morphism of schemes of finite presentation [def-sbc-locally-finite-presentation] with a $T$-action over $X$ for which $(y,t)\mapsto(y,yt)$ is an isomorphism $Y\times_kT\xrightarrow{\sim}Y\times_XY$ [def-pc-fibre-product]; faithfully flat means flat and surjective [def-weil-flat-morphism, def-weil-surjective-morphism]. Then every invertible $\mathcal O_Y$-module $L$ [def-sc-invertible-module] is isomorphic to $q^*N$ for some invertible $\mathcal O_X$-module $N$, where pullback means tensor inverse image [def-pc-module-pullback]. No injectivity of this pullback on isomorphism classes is asserted.

source.place: Tag 0BD9 (lemma-extend-invertible-module), applied to the open torus bundle in its associated product of projective-line bundles. Agent-extracted consequence, also using the Picard formula for projective bundles; the latter is WANTED in EGA II, projective bundles and invertible sheaves, and is not claimed to be part of 0BD9.

proof.text: Apply [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-frame-geometry] with $S=X$. Obtain $X=Y_0$, $Y_r\simeq Y$, and $q_j=p_ji_j:Y_j\to Y_{j-1}$, where $P_j=\mathbf P_{Y_{j-1}}(\mathcal O\oplus B_j)$ and $i_j$ is open. Every $P_j$ is smooth over $k$, and the first quotient summand trivializes $i_j^*\mathcal O_{P_j}(1)$. It suffices to descend an arbitrary line through each $q_j$.

source.place: Tags 023T and 05B2; coordinate-character construction and projective quotient chart specified in the frame-geometry node.

proof.text: Fix $1\leq j\leq r$ and a line $M_j$ on $Y_j$. By [lem-weil-pbc-smooth-scheme-over-field-regular], $P_j$ is locally Noetherian with regular local rings. Apply [lem-trf-regular-local-ufd-boundary-factorization] to each stalk with the empty parameter list ($r=0$ there): every stalk is a UFD, including all points outside $i_j(Y_j)$. Thus [lem-sfb-invertible-extension-factorial-complement] gives a line $\widetilde M_j$ on $P_j$ restricting to $M_j$.

Apply [lem-sfb-projective-bundle-picard-classification] to the rank-two module $\mathcal O\oplus B_j$. Obtain a line $M_{j-1}$ on $Y_{j-1}$ and a locally constant integer function $d_j$ with $\widetilde M_j\simeq\mathcal O_{P_j}(d_j)\otimes p_j^*M_{j-1}$. Pull back by $i_j$ using [lem-weil-pbc-module-pullback-tensor] and [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition]. The frame in [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-frame-geometry] trivializes every positive tensor power of $\mathcal O(1)$ and every dual power on this open. These trivializations glue across the disjoint level sets of $d_j$. Hence $M_j\simeq q_j^*M_{j-1}$.

source.place: Remark 4.2.7, printed p.75 (Picard decomposition); modules.tex Tag 01CD (lemma-tensor-product-pullback) and sheaves.tex Tag 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); restriction to the two-summand isomorphism locus.

proof.text: Start with $M_r=L$ on $Y_r\simeq Y$ and apply steps 2--3 successively for $j=r,r-1,\ldots,1$. Put $N=M_0$. The composition isomorphism of [lem-pc-module-pullback-identity-composition] identifies $q_r^*\cdots q_1^*N$ with $q^*N$, so $L\simeq q^*N$. For $r=0$, [lem-sfb-split-torus-torsor-frame-geometry] identifies $q$ with the identity; take $N$ to be $L$ under that isomorphism and use the identity-pullback clause. No uniqueness of $N$ is used.

source.place: Tag 0097 (lemma-push-pull-composition-modules); finite iteration of steps 2--3 and the identity case.

proof_origin.place: Tag 0BD9, combined with fpqc character descent and EGA II Remark 4.2.7; one-coordinate compactification argument by Q52.
